events_chronological: A girl is brought to a farm in the border states and chooses one of the men there for herself.
The man's mother is bought out of slavery by his extra labour and settles in a house outside a northern city.
A new owner the slaves nickname after his schooling arrives and starts measuring them and writing them up in a ledger.
The young woman overhears him instructing his nephews to list her animal characteristics on one side of the page and her human ones on the other.
The men at the farm lay a plan to run for it, and the plan falls apart.
The nephews hold her down in the barn and take her milk while her husband watches from the loft and loses his reason.
Pregnant and beaten, she walks north alone, and a white girl delivers her baby in a beached boat.
She reaches the house and has twenty-eight days of freedom, and her mother-in-law holds a feast for ninety people.
The owner comes to the house to take her and the children back.
She carries the children into the woodshed and cuts her elder daughter's throat with a handsaw.
She is jailed and released, her mother-in-law takes to her bed and dies, and the neighbours stop calling.
Her two sons run away from a house haunted by the dead baby.
One of the men from the farm arrives after eighteen years and drives the ghost out of the house.
A young woman walks out of the water, gives the dead child's name as her own, and comes to live with them.
The man is moved out of the house room by room and is finally taken to bed by the visitor in the shed.
An old friend shows him the newspaper cutting about the killing, and he leaves.
The visitor swells and consumes the mother, until thirty women come into the yard and sing until she is gone.
nonlinear_category_reason: No timeline dominates, the scenes do not fall into two alternating bands, and no non-temporal principle groups them into blocks; the order is associative, so none of the other six shapes applies. The killing at the centre is approached from a different direction each time it recurs, and the past arrives in fragments as the characters become able to bear it.
syuzhet_notes: The telling withholds the killing and approaches it repeatedly from different directions, so the same afternoon is entered five or six times before it is finished. Past and present interrupt each other mid-sentence with nothing to mark the change.
fabula_notes: The chronology is recoverable from the ages of the children and from the dated newspaper cutting, though the prose never lays it out in order.

events.content: Brought to the farm as a girl, she exercises the narrow choice available to her by selecting one enslaved man as partner.

reader: the mother's family begins under slavery at the farm

events.content: Years of extra labour purchase the older woman's release and establish a northern house as a possible destination beyond the farm.
events.location: the farm and a northern house

young mother: her mother-in-law has a free home in the north
reader: the northern house exists because of labour performed under bondage

events.content: Measurement, notebooks and pseudo-scientific scrutiny replace the previous management and turn every person into material for classification.

reader: a new owner applies systematic dehumanisation to the enslaved people

events.content: The owner's lesson asks his nephews to divide her features into animal and human columns, making the ideology behind their observation explicit.

young mother: the owner is recording her as partly animal
reader: the ledger formalises the violence the farm is preparing to enact

events.content: Signals and routes promise collective flight, but surveillance and mismatched timing break the plan before everyone can leave together.

reader: the group will have to face captivity and escape in fragments

events.content: They pin her in the barn while her husband watches from concealment, and the assault destroys his ability to act or later explain himself.

young mother: the nephews can violate her with the owner's authority
reader: the husband witnesses the assault and cannot intervene

events.content: Pregnant, beaten and alone, she walks until a white girl helps deliver the baby in a boat stranded away from the river.
events.location: roads north and a beached boat

reader: the mother's passage to freedom depends on aid from another young woman

events.content: Twenty-eight free days culminate in a lavish feast whose abundance strains neighbours already wary of unequal fortune.

reader: the family briefly experiences community and freedom at the northern house

events.content: The dead baby's attacks and their mother's refusal to abandon the address eventually drive both boys away from home.

reader: the household has been reduced to mother, surviving daughter and ghost

events.content: Eighteen years after the farm, a former companion enters the house, confronts its violent presence and imagines ordinary life can begin.

returning farm man: the house and mother remain governed by the dead child
reader: a survivor from the farm has returned to the mother's present

events.content: A fully grown young woman rises from water, takes the dead child's name and accepts shelter with an appetite that feels both helpless and possessive.

reader: the expelled haunting may have returned in bodily form

returning farm man: the mother killed her daughter when the owner came

events.content: As the visitor swells and the mother diminishes, thirty women restore the community withdrawn years earlier and drive the embodied haunting away.

reader: collective witness succeeds where private exorcism and denial failed
